items.text: Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, stated that the president's perspective is feminine and maternal, paying special attention to soft areas. She added that the presence of four women in the cabinet has highlighted issues such as details of social groups, the environment, and social matters.

Ahmad Alamolhoda stated in the Friday prayer sermon in Mashhad that the main strategy of the system is resistance and struggle. He emphasized that there should be no negotiations regarding nuclear technology. He also noted that the enemy no longer discusses nuclear issues in the negotiations to end the war.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, explained the image where she showed a heart with her hand. She said the heart she showed looked like a kidney and after learning from her niece, she did it again. She also responded to criticisms about this behavior and questioned why it should not be done in an official setting.

Mojtaba Khamenei announced in the Government Week message that any act harming social cohesion is forbidden. However, in a regime where factions accuse each other, this order is quickly violated. Implementing this order requires a ruler who can impose costs for disobedience, but Mojtaba Khamenei lacks his father's political background and influence.

Canada's Foreign Ministry condemned the threats against Iranian journalists abroad by the spokesperson of the Islamic Republic's armed forces. The ministry emphasized strong support for the right of media to operate freely and independently. This report was prepared by Mahsa Mortazavi.

In Iran, governmental methods to control citizens' behavior before actions occur have increased. These methods include summons, warnings, obtaining commitments, and threats of closure aimed at changing future behavior. This shift indicates a move from punishment after the act to preventive control of behaviors.

Al Arabiya reported that missiles launched from Iran were intercepted in northern Jordan. Images of the interception have been released. Earlier, channels close to the IRGC stated that missiles were launched from Isfahan, Kerman, and Kermanshah.

The US sanctioned Golden Global Bank and two affiliated companies in Turkey for facilitating tens of millions of dollars transfers for the Quds Force of the IRGC. The US Treasury described this as part of the 'economic expulsion' operation to cut off financial resources of the Islamic Republic. The bank enabled the transfer of Iran's oil revenues from China to Turkey.

A group of Iranians living in Germany gathered in Hamburg on Friday, 13 Shahrivar. The gathering was in protest against the executions by the Islamic Republic. Videos of this gathering have been sent to Iran International.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, stated on X that China seeks to strengthen common security, an approach supported by the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that regional countries should work to establish a regional security structure. Ghalibaf added that the Islamic Republic is ready to cooperate in this effort.

The US, UK, France, and Germany are negotiating to pass a resolution in the IAEA Board of Governors to report Iran's nuclear file to the UN Security Council. This follows a resolution from June accusing Iran of incomplete cooperation. Iran has not allowed inspectors to visit bombed nuclear sites.

The US State Department announced that the United States remains committed to cutting off the Islamic Republic's access to the international financial system and resources that it says are used to destabilize the region and threaten US interests and partners. The department said sanctions on Turkey-based Golden Global Bank are the latest action under the Economic Exclusion Operation and that facilitating Iran's illegal financial activities will have serious consequences. Washington said it will continue using diplomatic and economic tools to isolate the Islamic Republic until it stops supporting terrorism and destabilizing activities in the region.

Saman Taherpour said Keyvan Khosravani was one of the founders of combining modernism with authentic Iranian art and tradition. Khosravani introduced this approach to the world with the collaboration of Empress Farah. He used traditional Iranian arts in designing the official dresses of Empress Farah.

Axios, citing American officials and informed sources, reported that the Trump administration is developing a post-war strategy for Iran aimed at containing Iran and expanding normalization of Israel's relations with regional countries. Trump has held two meetings with senior advisors in recent weeks and has said in private conversations that he is working on 'something much bigger' in the Middle East. The three main pillars of the plan include regional alignment to contain Iran, advancing the next phase of the Gaza plan, and reaching a security agreement between Israel and Syria and implementing the Israel-Lebanon agreement.

Alireza Arafi stated that the US is unfamiliar with Iran's asymmetric and guerrilla warfare methods. He also mentioned the global hatred towards the US due to its oppressive actions. These remarks were made in Qom.

Donald Trump stated that there are no naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and that the US lost no personnel in its operation in Venezuela. He mentioned that the US might soon target 'Kuh Kolang Gazla' and that 18 people were killed in the conflict with Iran. Trump also said the US targeted the Islamic Republic's radars for the second time.

A woman in Tehran accused of acid attack on her landlord was sentenced to 15 years in prison and payment of blood money. The sentence was issued by the criminal court of Tehran province. More details were published by Harana News Agency.

Niloufar Majaver, a 27-year-old woman from Piranshahr, died after several days of hospitalization and being declared brain dead. Her family reported physical and sexual violence and deprivation of food and water before her hospital transfer. A complaint has been filed against a person related to the case, but no arrests have been made yet.

The audio version of program 24 with Fardad Farahzad discusses the empty docks of Iranian ports following US economic sanctions. This issue is presented as an economic challenge for Iran. The program examines the effects of these sanctions.

Research by Program 24 shows a sharp decline in activity at Shahid Rajaee and Imam Khomeini ports. Shahid Rajaee port, handling 85% of Iran's container trade, has been most affected. Increased insurance costs and the naval blockade have reduced commercial ship traffic.

Romania's Ministry of Defense announced the neutralization of an explosive device from a drone in the Black Sea. The bomb disposal team carried out the operation about five nautical miles east of the Sulina branch entrance. Romania, Bulgaria, and Turkey have neutralized over 150 drifting mines in the Black Sea and expanded their joint mine-clearing force.

Donald Trump mentioned the possibility of an attack on Mount Kalang Gezla, a site of important nuclear activities of the Islamic Republic. A military expert said the US can target the deep facilities in this area using bunker-buster bombs and B-2 aircraft. The expert also noted that missile attacks by the Islamic Republic on Jordan might push Jordan closer to the US.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, stated that the Islamic Republic is under full sanctions and facing economic death. He said Washington intends to economically strangle the Islamic Republic. US allies in the Persian Gulf and Europe also support this policy.

The Israeli army announced the clearance of tunnels leading to the Ali Al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon. It was reported that members of the IRGC are present in the area alongside Hezbollah forces. Additionally, the Islamic Republic has warned the US via Oman about Israel's capture of this area.

The spokesperson of Qatar's Foreign Ministry rejected the Islamic Republic's narrative about the attacks on Qatar, stating that official UN documents show Iranian missiles targeted civilian areas. Qatar's letters to the UN recorded damages and injuries. The spokesperson also confirmed the attack on Ras Laffan gas facilities and denied calling it an "alleged" attack.

Donald Trump stated that the US military may soon target underground facilities at Mount Kalang-Gazla in Iran. At the same time, the IRGC launched missile attacks on Jordan. The Trump administration is developing a strategic plan for the post-war period with the Islamic Republic.

The US has simultaneously sanctioned a bank and two Turkish financial companies. Siamak Javadi stated that the US is targeting the financial architecture of the Islamic Republic through secondary sanctions. These measures may lead to reduced foreign currency revenues and increased pressure on Iran's economy.

Ata Mohamad said that Israel's capture of Ali Al-Taher hill reduces Hezbollah's operational capabilities and gives Israel military superiority. This development may increase pressure on the Lebanese government to disarm Hezbollah. It also raises the likelihood of a long-term Israeli presence in the southern Lebanon buffer zone.

The 107th derby between Esteghlal and Persepolis was the first match between the two teams after the massacre of the Iranian people on January 8 and 9, 2026. Many martyrs of January were supporters of these two teams. Mazdak Mirzaei interviewed Mohammad Taghavi on the Hat-trick program.

Niloufar Majaver, a 27-year-old woman from Piranshahr, died after 10 days of severe physical and sexual abuse in an unknown location. Her family has filed a complaint against Ezzatodin Seyed Taheri, who is accused of the crime but has not been arrested yet. Reports indicate that this individual has abused other women as well.

Niloufar Majaver, a young woman from Piranshahr and Oshnavieh, was transferred to a hospital with severe injuries 10 days after leaving home and died from brain death. Her family holds a 41-year-old man responsible, but official investigations have not confirmed this. Reports differ on the details of the incident and Niloufar's personal information.

CENTCOM announced that US paratroopers have deployed communication equipment in a remote location in the Middle East. The exact location of the deployment was not disclosed. This action coincides with the ongoing extensive US military presence in the region.

Yemen's legitimate government forces have regained control of Saeed Taher Hill and the Dhayban area in Hayfan district from the Houthis. Military positions in the Al-Tuwair front in Taiz province were also recaptured, and the air force bombed Houthi positions. The Yemeni army reported that hundreds of Houthi militants were killed and wounded on the western coast.

TankersTrackers identified 17 ship-to-ship transfers of crude oil and gas in the Gulf of Oman on Friday. At least 24 million barrels of oil and petroleum products were moved in these transfers. Additionally, more oil tankers are waiting in the area to find other ships for transfer operations.

More than 120 people have been killed in Yemen after Houthi forces launched an operation to advance towards the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait. The clashes began with a ground attack supported by missile and drone strikes near the Red Sea coast. The Houthis are trying to strengthen their positions in this area.

On Friday evening, part of Kazemi Street in Isfahan subsided as a tanker passed. The tanker's wheels fell into the created hole. Firefighters and the water and sewage company managed to remove the tanker from the hole.

Two labor organizations condemned the shooting of job-seeking youth in Gachsaran and Ahvaz in a joint statement. They described the incident as part of labor suppression and widespread unemployment. They also warned that poverty and unemployment have become a serious crisis.

The New York Times reported that US government inspectors subjected about 50 members of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to lie detector tests in connection with leaks to journalists. The tests were conducted in August following reports of shortages of key munitions. A Pentagon spokesman declined to comment on the investigation but said the department takes leaks of classified information seriously.

Shahram Khaledi mentioned the possibility of a US attack on the Kooh Kalang nuclear site. He said the impact of such an attack depends on how it is carried out. Destroying underground equipment may require many bunker-buster bombs or special forces.

The drone war between Russia and Ukraine in the Black Sea has changed the security measures of ships. Oil tankers and cargo ships use nets and water tanks for protection. Ankara has entered negotiations with Russia and Ukraine to ensure maritime security in the region.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi stated that the US, UK, France, and Germany are trying to refer Iran's nuclear file back to the UN Security Council. He said this move is mostly symbolic and political. Practically, it will not bring any new measures beyond existing resolutions and sanctions.

Daneshjoo news agency reported that a small Islamic Republic oil tanker was attacked on Khark Island. The attack was carried out by the US military with a missile. There were no casualties, and no other sources have confirmed the report yet.

Mehdi Chamran, head of Tehran City Council, called for preemptive actions to disrupt the enemy's war formation and stated that a deterrent attack can be part of defense. He emphasized the creation of public shelters and designing multi-story parking lots to be usable as shelters in emergencies.

Students and parents report a sharp increase in tuition and school expenses for the new academic year. There are concerns about school safety and uncertainty about whether classes will be in-person or virtual. The Minister of Education has stated that charging fees in public schools is prohibited and that offending managers will be dismissed.

Mohammad Taghavi said in the Hattrick program that the 107th derby between Esteghlal and Persepolis was one of the few derbies that everyone was satisfied with. He attributed the many goal opportunities to the disorganized defense of both teams and their quick transition to attack. Fans, coaches, and players were all pleased with the match.

Simultaneously with the 107th derby between Esteghlal and Persepolis, families and associates of some martyrs of the Iranian National Revolution commemorated their loved ones who were killed by the Islamic Republic in December 2025. Among them were Amir Yektaei-Yeganeh, Mohammadjavad Rahimian, Akbar Hamzeh-Hosseini, and Mehrdad Moshtaqi. This commemoration included the release of images and explanations by Raha Pourbakhsh in the Hattrick program.

Saadoun Ghazali, a citizen of Mahabad, was arrested after attending the enforcement branch of the public and revolutionary prosecutor's office in the city. He was transferred to Mahabad prison to serve a one-year sentence.

Abbas Ghanbari's mother lit a candle in his memory by joining the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." Abbas Ghanbari, 37 years old, was killed by government agents in Shiraz on January 8, 2026. His mother called him a hero who will always be remembered.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated that economic problems are solvable and the Islamic Republic has achieved self-sufficiency in all fields. He said there is no need for foreign assistance in any scientific discipline. He also emphasized scientific cooperation with other countries.

The US Treasury Department sanctioned Golden Global Bank and two affiliated financial institutions in Turkey. These institutions facilitated financial transactions for the IRGC Quds Force. The US stated it will continue targeting financial institutions supporting the Islamic Republic.

The public relations of the Seyyed al-Shohada Corps in Tehran province announced that the explosion sound heard in Damavand was related to the educational exercise "Heydar Karar." These sounds were part of the pre-planned exercise activities. There was no prior announcement about this exercise.

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, announced that the city management aims to electrify all of Tehran. The city's energy needs can be met through solar power, local gas-based electricity production, and imported electricity. He also stated that Tehran is pursuing nuclear power and described this plan as a big win for the country.

Shayan Azadi's sister joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" and lit a candle. Shayan Azadi, 25, was killed by government agents during protests in Karaj on the evening of January 8. This act was done in memory of Iran's martyrs.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated that the December incidents were very severe and over three thousand people lost their lives. He said the list of casualties was announced under the guidance of Ali Khamenei. He also noted that the numbers announced by the enemy exceeded 30,000, and there were internal doubts about the accuracy of the 36,000 death figure.

A citizen protested the rising prices of medicines in a video. He addressed the government officials saying, "Death to all of you and death to the Islamic Republic." The video was sent to Iran International.

Ali Ahmadi, a retired teacher, has been detained in Adelabad Prison in Shiraz for nearly six months. He suffers from heart and kidney diseases and, despite medical confirmation of the need for specialized care, has been denied transfer to medical centers outside the prison. His medical condition and detention remain unresolved.

A video has been released showing a climber ascending Mount Damavand. The climb is dedicated to Yaser Modirroosta and other immortal figures of the National Iranian Revolution. Yaser Modirroosta was killed during the protests on January 8 in Gohardasht, Karaj.

The Football Federation's Disciplinary Committee fined Chadormalu Ardakan Club one billion tomans and ordered one match with only female spectators due to delays entering the field, throwing objects, and chanting against Tractor players. The ruling is not final and the club can appeal. Persepolis, Foolad, Esteghlal clubs and Gol Gohar's coach were also fined.

Dermot Gallagher, former Premier League referee, reviewed key scenes of Derby 107. He stated there was no foul or penalty in the incidents involving Saleh Hardani and Hossein Kanaani-Zadegan. The disciplinary committee must decide on Kanaani-Zadegan's suspension as neither the referee nor VAR saw the confrontation.

A man who intentionally ran over his wife with a car after she requested a divorce and demanded her dowry was arrested. The woman suffered fractures in parts of her body during the incident. The man was arrested and sent to prison.

Donald Trump announced that the US military may soon target underground facilities at Kuh-e Kelang in Iran. He said the US has taken control of Iran and targeted the Islamic Republic's military equipment in the Persian Gulf. Trump also confirmed the death of 18 American soldiers and stated that the Strait of Hormuz has been cleared of naval mines.

Viewers of Iran International have complained about a sharp increase in prices and shortages of essential goods such as medicine. They also criticize the inadequate insurance coverage. These issues have made it difficult for families to meet daily needs and access healthcare services.

The Israeli army captured the strategic heights of Ali al-Taher and Hezbollah's command tunnels. These attacks followed Hezbollah firing a drone towards Israeli forces in southern Lebanon. More details are provided in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Abulfazl Mirayiz, a victim of the revolutionary uprising in Gorgan, secretly provided monthly financial support to children with cancer. This was revealed to his family several months after his death. Mirayiz was killed on January 8 by gunfire from government forces.

The interrogation session of Pari Samani and Roya Samani, two sisters from Mahabad, was held at the first interrogation branch of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of the city. This session took place today.

The US dollar rate in Iran's free market reached an unprecedented 225,000 tomans. The prices of the euro, pound, and dirham were also traded at high levels. Additionally, the price of the Emami coin rose to 237 million tomans.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, the coach of Esteghlal, has permanently removed Saleh Hardani from the team due to his protests against decisions in Derby 107. Hardani is currently not allowed to train and had protested the choice of a free kick taker during the match. Mohammad Taghavi stated that this treatment was not appropriate for the team captain.

Masoud Pezeshkian called for a review of youth education methods at the opening ceremony of the first police high school. He emphasized that the education system is responsible for the problems young people face on the streets. Pezeshkian stressed the need to reconsider the approach to education.

Ali Shirazi from Iran International referred to Donald Trump's warning about the Kuh-e-Kalang facility. He said it seems the Islamic Republic continues its nuclear activities there. It is suggested that these activities may be related to nuclear bomb development.

Masoud Pezeshkian and Ahmadreza Radan inaugurated the first smart police boarding high school. This school was established to identify and train teenagers for the police force. Similar schools are planned to be opened in other provinces.

Al Arabiya, citing Yemeni military sources, reported that four Iranians and Lebanese were killed in an attack on a Houthi command center in Al-Jawf province. Yemeni military sources did not provide further details about the identities or roles of these individuals. The exact timing of the attack is unclear, but air and ground strikes occurred on September 4 and 5 in the area.

ILNA news agency reported on school dropout among children and adolescents in the border areas of West Azerbaijan. Poverty, long distances to schools, and lack of transportation services are cited as main factors. Experts warn that this situation may lead to increased poverty and social harm.

Simple medical drugs have become scarce and the black market for drugs has decreased. School tuition fees have become very expensive, and a power outage lasted for four hours in the Jeyhoon neighborhood of Tehran. Prices of items like corn and soy have increased sharply.

Alireza Panahian stated on Ofogh TV that those who avoid avenging the martyred leader are enemies of national interests. He emphasized that security cannot be ensured through fear and avoiding seeking revenge. Panahian also said officials must align themselves with the rhetoric of the people and the Imam regarding revenge.

The Fuman prosecutor stated that driving without an official license is illegal and offenders will be dealt with. This law also applies to riding motorcycles without a permit. Families were advised to supervise their children.

Masoud Pezeshkian said the Islamic Republic has failed to instill the belief in youth that they are the builders of the country's future. At the opening ceremony of the first police high school, he stated that the authorities, not the youth, are responsible for the problems young people face. Pezeshkian emphasized that proper education has not been provided to the youth.

The Football Federation's Disciplinary Committee has sentenced Chadormalu Ardakan Club to hold one home match with only female spectators. This ruling has been described as gender-biased. An interview was also conducted with Masoumeh Hasrati, a former player of Iran's women's national football team.

The governor of Qazvin announced a shortage of about 500 hospital beds in the province, stating that the per capita hospital bed ratio in Qazvin is 1.5 beds per thousand people. He also cited the dilapidation of medical equipment and infrastructure, a shortage of specialist doctors, and emergency medical personnel as other problems in the province's health sector.

Iran International has obtained three audio files of US military communications with the crew of the Stark 1 tanker. Hossein Aghaei analyzes that repeated CENTCOM attacks on tankers may indicate a change in the US military approach. The naval blockade has also moved closer to Iran's ports and islands.

A video obtained by Iran International shows US military radio warnings to the tanker STARK 1 before it was targeted near Kharg Island. Three warnings are heard via VHF channel, giving the crew time to evacuate. Islamic Republic media reported on Saturday morning that a tanker was targeted six miles from Kharg Island but did not name it.

Javad Mojabi, an Iranian poet and writer, passed away on Saturday, 14 Shahrivar after a period of illness. He was born in 1939 in Qazvin and was active in literature and visual arts. Mojabi collaborated with various publications and published several works.

The European Union stated it is ready to take further measures to protect its security and interests, including freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. The EU spokesperson said the union shares the US view on Iran's destabilizing activities and is concerned about Iran's military cooperation with Russia. The EU has imposed extensive sanctions on Iran and supports US economic pressure efforts to stop Tehran's destabilizing actions.

Artin Khajouy-Nia, a 16-year-old computer student, was killed by live gunfire during protests in front of the city hall of Qods on January 8, 2026. His mother shared a video of his shoes from different periods of his life as keepsakes. She called her son her eternal hero and expressed her lasting memory of him.

CENTCOM destroyed three IRGC oil tankers after two US warships were targeted by Iran. These tankers financed the IRGC and its proxy forces. CENTCOM's commander warned they will not hesitate to defend US forces.

Carlos Tevez plans to hold his farewell match in December this year at La Bombonera stadium. Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi may play together on the same team for the first time in this match. Tevez intends to form his main team from his closest friends.

The US Central Command released a video showing attacks by the IRGC on three oil tankers and two US Navy warships. Two tankers are out of service and one tanker was destroyed in the Gulf of Oman. These attacks followed ballistic missile launches.

Mohammad Baqer Kharazi, a detained cleric, has been summoned to the Special Clergy Prosecutor's Office due to reports sent against him by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other institutions. The concerns relate to his statements about domestic policy and hijab. The case is under investigation and the final decision rests with the judicial authority.

Ata Hosseinian explained the disagreements within the Islamic Republic government regarding the increase in gasoline prices. He said the government is forced to change the price and rationing due to the gasoline crisis. However, officials avoid taking responsibility for the social and political consequences of this decision.

Amid worsening economic crisis and security pressures, citizens have called for the fall of the government in messages to Iran International. They emphasize the need for street protests. Mohsen Mahimini explains the messages and officials' statements about a national revolution and repeated protests.

Nuzhat Mirrazi, the mother of two deceased protesters in Iran, was arrested in Lahijan and transferred to an unknown location. The arrest occurred one day after she released a video and amid increased security pressures in Gilan province. No information has been released about the detaining authority or possible charges.

The fleet development manager of the Road Maintenance Organization stated that out of 14,500 intercity buses, 8,600 are worn out and 3,000 are nearing wear. Additionally, 96% of active minibuses are worn out. There has been a more than 30% decrease in public transport passengers over the past three years.

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, said that the United States has no limits and will always demand more regardless of what it is given. He also stated that so far, the actions of the Americans regarding the JCPOA have been against their commitments.

Abolhasan Fatemi, Khamenei's representative in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, stated that in this critical historical period, the presence of clerics in gatherings and religious sessions has become more necessary. He emphasized that people pay attention to the number of clerics present at events and judge accordingly.

A group of Iranians in Nuremberg, Germany, commemorated the memory of the eternal names with a performance and gathering. The event took place on September 5th. Organizers introduced the eternal names and expressed support for the Iranian national revolution in Germany.

Tasnim news agency reported that an Iranian tanker was attacked by the US military near Khark Island on Saturday morning, September 4, with no casualties. It was also reported that two other tankers near Jask were attacked by the US. CENTCOM stated that after ballistic missile launches by the IRGC, US forces targeted three Iranian tankers, one of which was destroyed.

The US Embassy in Bahrain issued a security alert on Saturday, September 5, asking American citizens to exercise increased caution due to the possibility of an 'unforeseen escalation' of tensions in the Middle East. The embassy stated that the Islamic Republic and its affiliated groups may target US interests and American citizens worldwide. This warning was issued hours before the announcement of a US attack on three Iranian oil tankers.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported that several commercial ships in the northern Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman have been targeted by fire. These attacks occurred within the ongoing military activities in the region. The aim of the attacks was to disable the ships.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations announced that several commercial ships in the northern Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman were targeted by fire. The organization has received reports about these attacks but has not confirmed casualties or environmental impacts. Investigations are ongoing, and sailors are advised to follow security updates.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, described the December 1404 protests as the bitterest days of her career. She told Masoud Pezeshkian that despite no doubt about foreign interference, she does not really know the details of the matter. She also questioned how society reached a point where a security force member was martyred.
